Subject: [Status] us-west prefetch queue pressure — customer impact & temporary fallback

Hi Elena / ClearWave team,

Quick heads-up: we detected sustained prefetch queue pressure in our us-west (usw1) serving pool starting ~08:50 PT this morning. That pressure caused intermittent elevated p95 generation latency for streaming responses for a subset of prefetched routes — you may have seen elongated partial chunks or slightly delayed first tokens.

Immediate actions we've applied:
- Enabled a temporary routing fallback to a compatible us-east pool for prefetched routes from ClearWave traffic (this will increase cross-region egress for a small percentage of requests).
- Throttled aggressive prefetching on noisy keys to relieve KV/IO pressure while preserving steady-state throughput.

What you might observe:
- A small fraction (~3-5%) of prefetched requests temporarily routed to us-east with +20–40ms extra RTT.
- Short p95 spikes for streaming sessions started between 08:50–09:05 PT.

We're working the mitigation and will share a follow-up with the full timeline and next steps. If this routing change causes any unexpected behavior on your side (SDK errors, session affinity issues), please reply here and we will prioritize.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee

Elena — thanks for the patience. Short update and plan: 

What we observed (final):
- Timeline: elevated prefetch queue pressure between 08:50–11:10 PT.
- Impact: intermittent p95 latency elevation for streaming chunk arrival for a subset (~3–6%) of prefetched routes. No increased 5xx error rate observed.
- Root cause (high confidence): a combination of noisy prefetch keys from a small set of customers that triggered aggressive cache prefetch, coinciding with asynchronous KV eviction during a background maintenance job on the usw1 pool. The eviction increased IO pressure and caused momentary queueing in the prefetch workers.

Mitigations enacted:
- Temporarily routed affected prefetched routes to our us-east pool from 09:00–10:05 PT to reduce client impact.
- Throttled prefetch aggressiveness for identified noisy keys at 09:05 PT; reverted throttles after monitoring showed queue pressure normalized at 11:10 PT.
- Disabled the minor maintenance job that accelerated KV eviction; rescheduled it with lower priority for a later maintenance window.

Customer guidance:
- Retry behavior: we do not expect retry storms from the routing fallback. Session affinity was preserved for routed requests and we did not observe duplicate session tokens or retry amplification for ClearWave keys. If you have aggressive client-side retry windows <50ms, consider adding a small jitter to avoid coincident retries during short transient network events.

Next steps / follow-up:
- We will publish a short post-incident note and a more detailed postmortem (INF-9842) with timelines and mitigations. Draft is attached for internal review before customer publication.
- Engineering will propose a durable prefetch throttling policy that prevents a single tenant from triggering eviction cascades; ETA for policy proposal: 2 weeks.

Apologies for the disruption — we know consistency matters. I attached our internal draft post-incident note and the logs we captured for the period in question. Please let me know if you want us to host a short sync to walk through the timeline.

Best,
